ordered_pairing_radius_plateau.pdf: Operational two-radius pairing versus contour radius $R_0$ at several $\rho$, for both regulator classes. Shading marks the largest connected plateau found by the stated algorithm (adjacent nodes compatible when $|\Delta Y|\le 3\sigma + $ Cauchy--Green bound). Error bars are the standard error over independent named seeds. Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/ordered_pairing_grid.csv.
predarboux_pairing_vs_width.pdf: $\epsilon_{\rm leak}$ (operational two-radius) versus feature width, grouped by Laurent cutoff, for both regulator classes. Points and bars are the mean and standard error over ten independent named seeds. Dashed grey: the $N^{-1/2}$ random-feature guide; dotted: the fitted width exponent. Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/predarboux_convergence_seed_rows.csv.
raw_virasoro_vs_width.pdf: raw Sugawara residual $R_{\rm raw}$ (filtered-Fock) versus feature width, grouped by Laurent cutoff, for both regulator classes. Points and bars are the mean and standard error over ten independent named seeds. Dashed grey: the $N^{-1/2}$ random-feature guide; dotted: the fitted width exponent. Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/predarboux_convergence_seed_rows.csv.
predarboux_sampling_error_vs_width.pdf: $\|\omega^{(N)}-\omega^{\rm ana}\|_F/\|\omega_{\rm can}\|_F$ versus feature width, grouped by Laurent cutoff, for both regulator classes. Points and bars are the mean and standard error over ten independent named seeds. Dashed grey: the $N^{-1/2}$ random-feature guide; dotted: the fitted width exponent. Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/predarboux_convergence_seed_rows.csv.
architecture_controls_predarboux.pdf: Architecture controls, panel (a) radial / pre-Darboux. Bars are means over independent named seeds with standard-deviation whiskers; hatched bars marked '0' are exact floating-point zeros drawn at an off-scale floor rather than on the log axis. Panel (c) is a non-discriminating implementation check (Proposition 3.5). Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/architecture_controls_seed_rows.csv.
architecture_controls_ward.pdf: Architecture controls, panel (b) chiral Ward test. Bars are means over independent named seeds with standard-deviation whiskers; hatched bars marked '0' are exact floating-point zeros drawn at an off-scale floor rather than on the log axis. Panel (c) is a non-discriminating implementation check (Proposition 3.5). Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/architecture_controls_seed_rows.csv.
architecture_controls_postdarboux.pdf: Architecture controls, panel (c) post-Darboux implementation check. Bars are means over independent named seeds with standard-deviation whiskers; hatched bars marked '0' are exact floating-point zeros drawn at an off-scale floor rather than on the log axis. Panel (c) is a non-discriminating implementation check (Proposition 3.5). Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/architecture_controls_seed_rows.csv.
darboux_admissibility_vs_width.pdf: Physical admissibility of the canonicalizing map versus feature width (appendix C). Panel (a): the involution defect of eq. (3.32) on a log axis. Panel (b): the minimum eigenvalue of the induced positive-frequency Gram form on a LINEAR axis, since it is signed; the dashed line is zero, above which a normalizable Fock vacuum exists. Bars are standard errors over independent named seeds. Estimator class: exact_symbolic. Source: results/jhep_frozen/darboux_physical_admissibility.csv.
sampled_tt_central_charge.pdf: Sampled $\langle TT\rangle$ central charge with block standard errors over independent named seeds (blue: Wick-factorized, with the Gaussian factorization disclosed as an analytic input; red: fully direct four-field Monte Carlo). Dashed line: the free-boson value $c=1$. Estimator class: sampled_finite_network. Source: results/jhep_frozen/sampled_tt_central_charge.csv.
sampled_ward_convergence.pdf: Sampled finite-network stress Ward error versus the number of independent realizations $M$, for the neutral 2-, 3- and 4-vertex configurations. Bars are block standard errors over independent named seeds; the guide is the $M^{-1/2}$ Monte Carlo rate. Estimator class: sampled_finite_network. Source: results/jhep_frozen/sampled_ward_summary.csv.
ward_controls.pdf: Ward controls at the largest $N$ and $M$: the chiral/angular test separates the selected architecture from the radial and angular controls. Bars are block standard errors over independent seeds. Estimator class: sampled_finite_network. Source: results/jhep_frozen/sampled_ward_summary.csv.
ns_pairing_convergence.pdf: Pre-canonicalization Neveu--Schwarz pairing convergence: raw CAR defect and fermionic leakage versus feature width, with block standard errors over independent named seeds and the $N^{-1/2}$ guide. Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/ns_frozen_metrics.csv.
ns_super_virasoro_residuals.pdf: Raw and canonicalized $\mathcal N=1$ super-Virasoro residuals. Exact floating-point zeros are drawn at an off-scale floor and labelled '0'. Estimator class: deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/ns_frozen_metrics.csv.
raw_modewise_central_charge_offset_model: Extended modewise anomaly ratio $c_m$. Squares: the exact_symbolic null from the canonical truncated Sugawara algebra. Circles: the raw empirical finite-feature measurement with seed standard errors. Dashed: the legacy one-parameter alternating offset model. Estimator class: exact_symbolic + deterministic_finite_feature. Source: results/jhep_frozen/central_offset_mode_extension.csv.
sampled_vertex_weights.pdf: Sampled vertex-operator weights with block standard errors over independent named seeds, against the theory curve $h_a=a^2/2$. Estimator class: sampled_finite_network. Source: results/jhep_frozen/sampled_vertex_weights.csv.
finite_width_cumulant.pdf: Connected fourth cumulant of the neural field versus width, with block standard errors, the fitted exponent, and the exact finite-width prediction $\kappa_4=-3\sigma_\phi^4/(8N)$. Interpreted only as finite-width non-Gaussianity. Estimator class: sampled_finite_network. Source: results/jhep_frozen/finite_width_cumulant.csv.
